# Part IX: Applying the Toolkit {.unnumbered}

The earlier parts taught the techniques one by one. Real audit problems seldom fit a single technique. This part takes an audit area and brings together everything that helps with it, from simple counts to association rules, networks, record linkage and machine learning.

It begins with the accounts. Journal entries are where management can override controls, and auditing standards on fraud require them to be tested. The first chapter tests every entry in a general ledger. The second reconciles records that should agree, such as the cash book and the bank statement, and checks claims against independent records.

Public procurement follows. Tenders are where a great deal of public money is spent, and where competition can be quietly restricted or rigged. The first of these chapters checks the tendering process itself, with red flags that work for every tender. The next two look for bid rigging, where firms that should compete secretly decide who will win.

After the award comes payment. The payables chapter follows a department's purchases from the vendor master to the payment.

The part ends with a whole scheme audited from start to end. It gathers what earlier chapters found about one health insurance scheme, and builds a case from several independent sources.

The chapters draw on many earlier ones, so read them after Parts I to VIII, or at least after the chapters they point to.
